note: Look, not law. Absorb or drop next sitting. A spark is not a trap.

items.claim: A control-plane sitting is one class of work; a second class is a split.
items.whyNotLaw: No check yet that a multi-repo transcript fails a sitting.

items.claim: A wall-clock is not a control-plane fuse.
items.whyNotLaw: Named decay signs already cover rot; hours would be an invented clock.
items.because: T25 already names decay signs. A wall-clock would be a second clock.

items.claim: A hosted or private-index code search that returns zero is not a ZERO.
items.whyNotLaw: The search product is not a container. GitHub search of Virbos was empty; the objects were not.

items.claim: A control plane that will issue or drop reads factory/CONTROL_PLANE.md.
items.whyNotLaw: successorReads names sparks but not CONTROL_PLANE.md; CONSOLE does. Drift, not yet a check.

items.claim: An owner paste of a missed spark is a lead, not law.
items.whyNotLaw: No check that a successor treated a chat paste as AGENTS.
items.because: T50 already rules that the repository is the record and a fact from chat or notes is a diary; a second row would be the same law twice.

items.claim: A session that confirms it understands still invents and leaves the loop; reading files or alumni is not a hold.
items.whyNotLaw: Landing checks do not read chat. No command fails a spoken confirmation. Until a return must paste a command or omit, absorbing this is a diary.

items.claim: A return validates spendUsd and cachedTokens and then discards the row, so no command sums spend or cache hits across lanes.
items.whyNotLaw: Returns so far are prose in lane logs; a store with no rows is a fixture, and the cap it would enforce has no dated row in factory/decisions.json.
